messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acmehealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: POC prompt dataset collection & next steps

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment for the POC / trial: 

Summary of what we discussed
- Goal: validate Redwood can meet ACME Health's retrieval & response quality for clinician-facing triage assistant (reduction in task time + high intent accuracy).
- Scope: a 3-week POC focusing on prompts and historical logs to build an eval set; model/latency tuning on Redwood hosted/dedicated infra.

Proposed success criteria (to confirm)
- Intent match >= 85% on the eval set (tiered by intent importance)
- Hallucination rate < 2% on flagged clinical-response queries
- Semantic similarity score (human-reviewed) meets ACME baseline on sampled cases
- P50 latency <= 150ms, P95 <= 500ms for single-turn inference on the selected model variant

What we need from ACME to run the eval
1) Prompt set + example responses: a CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output (if available), source (ui/logs), timestamp, anonymized_user_id. Aim for ~200-500 representative prompts to start; we can expand later.
2) Historical logs / edge cases: anonymized logs of 3–5k recent interactions (or a representative subset) — if PHI is present, please apply the redaction checklist (see below).
3) Ownership & transfer method: who will own the data upload (Sana / Tom?), and how will you share (S3 presigned link, secure SFTP, or upload to our secure Drive)?

Proposed timeline
- Data deliverable (sample prompts + any logs): target March 6
- Baseline run & initial metrics: March 9–11
- Full eval & human review: March 12–18
- Review sync & decision: week of March 22 (final decision by March 25)

Attachments: I’m attaching a prompt_samples.csv (small stub) and a draft poc-eval-plan docx that outlines the evaluation rubric and metrics.

Can you confirm: 1) who will own the upload at ACME, 2) whether PHI redaction is needed and who will perform it, and 3) if the March 6 target for the first data drop works?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min handoff call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-call: POC prompt dataset collection & next steps — Eval plan + data format

Thanks Alicia — really helpful. I’ve attached the formal POC evaluation plan (poc-eval-plan-acmehealth.docx) that maps success criteria to test cases and ownership. Key highlights below and a few asks to keep things moving: 

Evaluation rubric (summary)\- Quality metrics: intent match (automated + human spot-check), top-1 answer accuracy when an expected_output exists, factual accuracy / hallucination flag rate, and human-assigned relevance score on sampled cases.
- Safety: detection of PHI/hallucination on clinical answers; any high-risk hallucination events escalate to manual review.
- Performance: p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 500ms for standard prompt lengths (<= 256 tokens).

Concrete asks / data format details\1) Prompt CSV template (attached) — please ensure these columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output (optional), source, timestamp (ISO8601), anonymized_user_id, priority_flag (low/med/high).
2) If you can include a small set of 20–30 edge-case transcripts (free-text) that historically caused failures, that will help us validate safety/regression.
3) For logs: provide JSONL or CSV with anonymized identifiers and a mapping of event_type, raw_prompt, system_response, and any human labels (if available).

POC milestone timeline (updated)\- Mar 6: sample prompts + format confirmed (if you need more time, Mar 8 is ok — let us know)\- Mar 9–11: baseline runs + automated metric pass\- Mar 12–18: human review + safety checks (we’ll provide a short UI for annotation)\- Mar 19–20: results review and go/no-go discussion\- By Mar 25: decision / next-phase recommendation

Security & transfer
- We can accept S3 presigned URLs or secure SFTP. If PHI is present please share confirmation of redaction steps and any compliance docs. We’re happy to sign an additional DPA amendment if needed.

Can Alicia / Tom / Sana confirm: 1) final upload date (Mar 6 vs Mar 8), 2) transfer method (S3 presigned link or SFTP), and 3) who will be our point-of-contact for dataset follow-up (Sana?). 

Linking resources: HubSpot deal and the shared drive folder are in the attached related_links for convenience.

Thanks — I’ll block time for the results review on March 19 pending data delivery.

Warmly,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachments: poc-eval-plan-acmehealth.docx, prompt_samples.csv
